note: 40 hook formulas. Merged from Serge Bulaev's 20 (F1-F20, with 2026 reach notes) and Jake Schincariol's 21 (with traps), deduplicated, plus 7 formats from the creators in voice.md. Examples show the shape only: some numbers are the original authors' and some are illustrative. Never reuse an example's number in a draft. Goal = what the post mainly earns. Caution 'care' = read note_2026 before using.
rules: Pick by goal first, then by topic.
Never blend two hooks in one post.
Line 1 is never a question. If the best hook is a question, invert it into the number that answers it and move the question to the close.
Don't use the same hook twice in 7 days.
The density rule in rules.md applies on top of every template.

hooks.name: Contrarian + Receipts
hooks.template:
Everyone says {common advice}. After {specific experience with a number}, I think that's wrong.

[2-6 dated receipts or data points]

[What actually works instead, stated plainly]

[Specific closing question]
hooks.example: Everyone says post daily. I posted 4x a week for a year and beat every daily poster in my niche.
hooks.best_for: Taking a position. Highest comment rate.
hooks.trap: Being contrarian about something nobody believes. The belief has to be genuinely common.
hooks.note_2026: Dated receipts are the best protection a post can have. Use one contrast only: either 'what died wasn't X, it was Y' or an 'if you're still X' close, never both.

hooks.name: R.I.P. Obituary
hooks.template:
R.I.P. {category or habit}.

Cause of death: {specific mechanism + number}.

[2-3 paragraphs of dated evidence]

I {defended / did} {old thing} until {dated event}.

Under the hood, {N} things changed:
1. [change + number]
...

[One-line close]
hooks.example: R.I.P. the 40-slide pitch deck for pre-seed.
hooks.best_for: Era-ending claims, 'the game changed' posts.
hooks.trap: Declaring something dead that's still working for most of your readers. They'll say so.
hooks.note_2026: 'The winners aren't X, they're Y' close is a contrast; fine once, so don't open with one too.

hooks.name: Before / After
hooks.template:
{Time ago / last year}, I {low state with a number}.

{Now / this year}, I {high state with a number}.

[Line 3: the first concrete number of the change]

The difference was {one lever}.

[How the lever works, 3-5 lines]

[Mirror question: what's your {before}→{after}?]
hooks.example: 18 months ago I was writing proposals at 2am. Today I send them in 6 minutes. One template did it.
hooks.best_for: Proof you've travelled the distance your reader wants to travel.
hooks.trap: Three-part transformations. Name one lever or the reader stops believing you.
hooks.note_2026: Number-first by construction. Never open line 3 with 'Here's what changed'.

hooks.name: Time-Anchor Confession
hooks.template:
{N} {days/months} ago, I stopped {behaviour}.

[Line 2: the first consequence, with a number]

[Why the old behaviour seemed to work]

[The quiet cost]

[New behaviour, what dropped, what surprised you]

[Mirror question: what did you stop that made your work better?]
hooks.example: On 14 March I stopped answering DMs within the hour. Replies fell 41%. Clients got better.
hooks.best_for: A real reset, a habit you dropped.
hooks.trap: Manufactured vulnerability. Readers can tell, and now they report it.
hooks.note_2026: The confession must be a specific, dated, uncomfortable fact with no 'let me be honest' frame, and the substance must land in the first 3 lines.

hooks.name: Mistake Cost
hooks.template:
{Specific cost: money, hours, marks, a round} is what {one mistake} cost me.

[What happened, dated]

[What I do now, as exact steps]

[The resource or check that would have saved me]

[Question: what's the check you added after your worst mistake?]
hooks.example: $18,000 is what not having a contract cost me last March.
hooks.best_for: Trust. People forward the posts where you look bad. Core of the 'nobody told me' format.
hooks.trap: A fake-humble mistake. 'I cared too much' reads as a brag and kills the post.
hooks.note_2026: Real failure in the first 3 lines outperforms polished framing. State the cost flat, no candor announcement.

hooks.name: Self-Proving Test
hooks.template:
{Claim with a number}.

Not because {common reason}. Because {real reason}.

So here's the test. For the next {timeframe}, I will {specific commitment}.

You do two things:
1. [substantive action]
2. [verification action]

If I'm right, {outcome}. If I'm wrong, I'll post the numbers anyway.
hooks.example: Most posts die in the first 30 minutes. For the next 24 hours I'll reply to every comment within 5.
hooks.best_for: Tests in public, building-in-public experiments.
hooks.trap: Making a promise you won't keep. Someone will check.
hooks.note_2026: The two reader actions must be real (verify a number, report a result), never 'comment YES'. 'Not because X. Because Y.' is this post's one contrast.

hooks.name: Steal This
hooks.template:
Here's the (exact) {template / prompt / checklist / repo} I used to {specific outcome with a number}. Copy it.

[The whole thing, in the post or a carousel]

[How to use it in 2-3 lines]

[Question about the reader's situation]

P.S. {Editable copy / link} is in the first comment. Free.
hooks.example: Here's the exact 4-line email I used to reopen 3 dead deals. Steal it.
hooks.best_for: Lead magnets without the gate. Highest conversion format.
hooks.trap: Making them ask for something you could have posted. Give the artifact away in the post.
hooks.note_2026: Never 'comment X to get Y': that's the phrasing the March 2026 update targets and readers report. Put the file in the first comment and say so.

hooks.name: Receipt / Ledger
hooks.template:
{Odd, unrounded number}.

[One line: what this number covers]

Every line item, nothing rounded:
- {item}: {number}
- {item}: {number}
...

[What it replaces or compares to]

[What surprised you: what broke, what worked]
hooks.example: {{₹ cost}} and {{N}} hours. That's what shipping my first open-source app cost.
hooks.best_for: Build logs, cost breakdowns, 'what it actually took'. The strongest 2026 opener.
hooks.trap: A receipt with no story. The number opens the door, the story is the room. And never round or invent a figure.
hooks.note_2026: Odd-precision number in line 1 is the biggest positive first-line signal (+34% median likes, vendor data).

hooks.name: Paid vs Free
hooks.template:
{People pay / I paid} {amount} for {thing}.

Today it's free.

The exact {N}-step {named framework}:
1. {STEP}: [concrete instruction]
...

[Run it today. Most people find {N} fixes in {time}.]
hooks.example: Bootcamps charge {{price}} for this Claude Code setup. Here it is free.
hooks.best_for: Giving away a framework that's genuinely worth money.
hooks.trap: Steps that are vague imperatives ('be customer-obsessed'). Each step must be something you can do with your hands.
hooks.note_2026: Highest baseline multiplier in Serge's set (19.64x). Steps must not be 'Stop X, start Y' lines.

hooks.name: The Comparison
hooks.template:
{Expensive or popular option} vs {cheap or unpopular option}. {Surprising verdict}.

[Same task, both ways, with numbers]

[What the expensive option genuinely does better]

[When you'd pick each]
hooks.example: A $12,000 brand agency vs a $20 tool and a weekend. The weekend won.
hooks.best_for: Tool and process posts. Very high share rate.
hooks.trap: An unfair comparison. Concede what the expensive option genuinely does better.
hooks.note_2026: The comparison is the post's one contrast.

hooks.name: Curiosity Gap
hooks.template:
The {superlative} {thing} I ever {did} {broke the obvious rule}.

[Line 3, before the fold: the specific reveal with a number or name]

[One sensory anchor]

[What it means]

[Closing question]
hooks.example: The best hire I ever made failed the interview.
hooks.best_for: Openers that earn the 'see more' tap.
hooks.trap: A gap you never close. Pay it off by line 3 or you've written clickbait.
hooks.note_2026: Teaser phrases ('what nobody tells you', 'the real question is') are on every AI-tell list. The gap must be specific and close inside the first 140-210 characters.

hooks.name: Story Cold Open
hooks.template:
"{The real line of dialogue}"

{Who said it, when, and why it mattered, with a date or number}.

[3-6 short present-tense lines inside the scene]

[The turn: what changed, what it cost]

[One line of meaning, not a moral]
hooks.example:
"We're going with someone cheaper."

That email arrived 40 minutes after I sent my best proposal of the year.
hooks.best_for: Story posts. Highest dwell time.
hooks.trap: Dialogue nobody would say, or stakes you made up. Use the real line, including the ugly parts.
hooks.note_2026: Specifics (a date, a place, a number, a name) in the first two lines are what separate real vulnerability from the 'false vulnerability' trope. Never all-caps the first line.

hooks.name: Permission Slip
hooks.template:
You're allowed to {specific thing your reader feels guilty about}.

[One dated fact from your own record that earns the permission]

[What happened when you allowed it]

[Soft close]
hooks.example: You're allowed to skip a hackathon to finish one project properly.
hooks.best_for: Reach beyond your niche.
hooks.trap: Generic self-care. It must be specific to your reader's working life, and you must believe it.
hooks.note_2026: Visibly formulaic. Max once a month, one permission (not three), and it needs a dated fact from your own record.

hooks.name: Bait and Switch
hooks.template:
No more {beloved habit / standard practice}.

I'm also cutting {second thing}.

[Beat of suspense]

[The reveal: it's an upgrade, with a number]

[The value underneath the change]
hooks.example: No more to-do lists. I'm also cutting my Notion dashboard.
hooks.best_for: A process change that's secretly an improvement.
hooks.trap: A real loss dressed up as good news. The comments will catch it.
hooks.note_2026: Write the reveal as a plain sentence with a number. No 'Plot twist:' bridge.

hooks.name: Named Gratitude
hooks.template:
To {Name} and {Name}: thank you for {the specific thing}.

[What each person actually did, one concrete act each]

[Why it mattered to the work]

[Close that honours them, not you]
hooks.example: To {{Name}} and {{Name}}, who reviewed my first {{N}} pull requests line by line: thank you.
hooks.best_for: Mentors, teammates, the people behind a win. Celebrating others travels.
hooks.trap: Name-dropping to borrow reach. Readers see through it.
hooks.note_2026: Give each person one concrete act, not a one-word quality ('the vision, the grit, the heart' is the triple tell).

hooks.name: Explain Like I'm 5
hooks.example: PRD vs BRD vs MRD, explained like you're in first year.
hooks.best_for: Demystifying jargon. Saved and reshared as a reference.
hooks.trap: Getting it wrong or sounding condescending. Both destroy authority.
hooks.note_2026: Line 1 is a statement, not 'What is X?'.

hooks.name: Status Strip
hooks.template:
On paper, I'm {impressive label}.

In reality, {the humbling moment, specific}.

[The scene]

[What the contrast taught you, in 1-2 lines]
hooks.example: On paper I shipped an e-commerce store for a wholesale business. In reality, day one was {{the real humbling moment}}.
hooks.best_for: Self-roast posts. Turns credibility into warmth.
hooks.trap: A humble-brag. The setup must genuinely deflate.
hooks.note_2026: 'On paper / in reality' is the post's one contrast. Put one real detail in the humbling scene.

hooks.name: Controlled A/B
hooks.template:
{Action A} → {outcome A with a number}.
{Same action, one thing changed} → {opposite outcome B with a number}.

Same {constant}. Same {constant}. The only difference was {variable}.

[What you first thought it meant]
[What it actually shows]

[Question that makes the reader test their own variable]
hooks.example: Launched {{app}} with a landing page → {{N}} signups. Relaunched it with a 30-second demo video → {{N}}.
hooks.best_for: One variable flipped the outcome. Reads as evidence, not opinion.
hooks.trap: Changing two things. Then it's a story, not a comparison.
hooks.note_2026: The A/B is the contrast. Don't add an 'it's not the tool, it's the brief' line on top.

hooks.name: False Binary
hooks.template:
Everyone reaches for one of two answers to {problem}.

{Option A}? {Why it fails.}
{Option B}? {Why it fails.}

Both fail for the same reason: {shared flaw}.

So I tried a third: {concrete option}.

[How it works, 2-3 lines with numbers]

[Question: A, B, or something else?]
hooks.example: Every fresher picks either 'learn everything' or 'specialise early'. Both fail for the same reason.
hooks.best_for: Strategy posts where both obvious answers are wrong.
hooks.trap: A strawman. A and B must be what readers really reach for.
hooks.note_2026: Structurally a contrast plus a triple. Only use it when the third option is concrete, and never pair it with H21 in the same post.

hooks.name: Anecdote Meets Evidence
hooks.example: My last {{N}} posts with a number in line 1 got {{N}}x the comments. Turns out that's measured already:
hooks.best_for: Personal noticing backed by real data.
hooks.trap: Invented or unsourced stats. Use H05 instead if you don't have evidence.
hooks.note_2026: Three sourced numbers are the safe kind of triple. No 'Here's what the data says' bridge.

hooks.name: Diverging Curves
hooks.template:
[Two things that look the same today]

{Approach A}: {what it does over time}.
{Approach B}: {the opposite}.

Month one, {X}. Month six, {Y}.

{One-line maxim}
hooks.example: Courses give you certificates. Projects give you stories. Month one, same CV. Month six, only one gets interviews.
hooks.best_for: A closing move, or a short quotable post.
hooks.trap: Forcing it on two things that don't actually diverge.
hooks.note_2026: The maxim is the one contrast. Short standalone posts miss the length lift; fine as a close for H18 or H08.

hooks.name: Anaphora Stack
hooks.template:
{Thing 1} can {bad outcome} {timing}.
{Thing 2} can {bad outcome} for {reason}.
[3-4 more parallel lines, escalating]

[One real anecdote with a number]

[The real asset, stated plainly]

So I changed how I work:
- [tactic]
- [tactic]

[Personal-audit question]
hooks.example: Placements can get delayed. Offers can get revoked. Startups can shut down in a month.
hooks.best_for: Risk and dependency arguments.
hooks.trap: Framing LinkedIn itself as bad, inside a LinkedIn post.
hooks.note_2026: The repetition run is the post's one stacked device. State the reframe directly, no 'Here's what most people miss'.

hooks.name: Experiment Result
hooks.template:
I {did thing} for {N} {days/weeks}. {Result in numbers}.

[Setup: why and how]

[What happened, with numbers]

[What I'd change]
hooks.example: I sent 400 cold DMs in 30 days. 11 replied. 2 became clients.
hooks.best_for: Challenges, experiments, anything countable.
hooks.trap: Burying the number. It goes in line 1 or the formula does nothing.
hooks.note_2026: Number-first by construction.

hooks.name: List Promise
hooks.template:
{N} things I wish someone had told me before {milestone}.

1. [specific, actionable]
...

[Which one cost you the most to learn]
hooks.example: 7 things I wish someone had told me before I shipped my first open-source app.
hooks.best_for: Saves.
hooks.trap: N above 10. The reader doesn't believe you have 15 good ones, and you don't.
hooks.note_2026: Each item needs a specific. Ten vague items is the slop pattern.

hooks.name: Insider View
hooks.template:
After {N months/rounds/projects} {doing thing}, here's the part nobody puts in the {course / JD / brochure}.

[The specific thing]

[Proof from your own experience]
hooks.example: After 3 case competitions, here's the part the problem statement never tells you.
hooks.best_for: Credentialed takes. Works only if the experience is real.
hooks.trap: Promising a secret and delivering common knowledge. The comments will say so.
hooks.note_2026: 'Nobody tells you' phrasing is on AI-tell lists. Name the specific thing in line 2 to survive it.

hooks.name: The Callout
hooks.template:
If you're still {doing outdated thing}, {specific cost}.

[Why it stopped working, with a date or number]

[What to do instead, exact steps]
hooks.example: If you're still writing every line by hand before you prototype, you're paying for it in weeks.
hooks.best_for: Short posts with one instruction.
hooks.trap: Calling out something nobody does, or calling out your own audience with contempt.
hooks.note_2026: Avoid the 'Stop X, start Y' wording (-6.7%). Name the cost instead.

hooks.name: Scenario
hooks.template:
You're in a {customer call / investor meeting / code review}. {The exact question or situation}.

[What most people do]

[What actually works, in numbered steps]

[Specific closing question]
hooks.example: You're on a call with your first paying customer. They ask: "Why should I trust a 4-person team?"
hooks.best_for: Founder and builder thinking in public. Very high comment volume.
hooks.trap: A scenario with one obvious answer. There has to be a real fork.
hooks.note_2026: Open with the scenario as a statement. The question to the reader goes at the close, not in line 1.

hooks.name: Myth Bust
hooks.template:
{Popular explanation} isn't why {bad outcome}.

[The real cause, with a number]

[How to check it in your own case]

[The fix]
hooks.example: Your idea isn't why nobody's using your app.
hooks.best_for: Reframing a common belief.
hooks.trap: Busting the myth and never naming the replacement. Name it in line 2.
hooks.note_2026: This is an 'it's not X' frame, so it's the post's only contrast.

hooks.name: Tiny Hook
hooks.example: my bad.
hooks.best_for: Light, relatable posts. Stops the scroll with whitespace.
hooks.trap: Overuse. Once a month, or it reads as a tic. And it still needs one useful line.
hooks.note_2026: Counts as one of your 2 fragments for the post.

hooks.name: The Warning
hooks.template:
{Common practice} is costing you {specific thing your reader cares about}.

[How, with a number]

[The fix, in the same post]
hooks.example: Your 'quick call to align' is costing you six hours a week.
hooks.best_for: Readers who haven't connected cause to cost.
hooks.trap: Fear with no exit. Give the fix in the same post.
hooks.note_2026: Drop the word 'quietly' (a 2026 tell).

hooks.name: Good vs Great
hooks.template:
Good {role}s {do X}. Great {role}s {do Y}.

[An example of Y from real work]

[How to practise Y]
hooks.example: Good builders ship the feature. Great builders delete the one nobody used.
hooks.best_for: Quotable one-liners.
hooks.trap: A distinction that's just 'try harder'. Y must be a different action.
hooks.note_2026: This is the post's one contrast.

hooks.name: Time Saved
hooks.template:
{Task} used to take me {long time}. It now takes {short time}.

[The exact system, as steps]

[What it can't do]
hooks.example: Writing a week of posts used to take me 5 hours. It now takes 20 minutes.
hooks.best_for: Tool, system and automation posts. Your Claude Code workflows.
hooks.trap: An unbelievable ratio. 5 hours to 20 minutes lands. 5 hours to 8 seconds doesn't.
hooks.note_2026: Number-first by construction.

hooks.name: Personal Rule
hooks.template:
I don't {widely accepted practice}. Ever.

[Why, with a cost you paid]

[What I do instead]
hooks.example: I don't start a project without a kill date.
hooks.best_for: Positioning. Attracts the right people by repelling the wrong ones.
hooks.trap: A rule you break constantly. Someone in the comments will know.
hooks.note_2026: Fine. Don't preface it with 'Unpopular opinion:'.

hooks.name: The Walk-Away
hooks.template:
I {quit / dropped / killed / deleted} {valuable thing}. {Result}.

[What it cost]

[Why it was right anyway]
hooks.example: I killed {{project}} {{N}} weeks before launch. {{Other project}} shipped {{N}} days earlier because of it.
hooks.best_for: Values posts with a result attached.
hooks.trap: Walking away at no cost. Name what it cost or it reads as theatre.
hooks.note_2026: Fine.

hooks.name: Chaos Log
hooks.template:
{N} things on my plate this {week/month}. Here's how each one is actually planned.

- {project}: {next step} by {day}
- ...

[The system that makes it work, 2-4 steps]

[One thing I dropped and why]

[Question]
hooks.example: {{N}} things on my plate this week and I'm dropping none of them.
hooks.best_for: Your signature weekly format. Organised chaos, made visible.
hooks.trap: Turning it into a flex list. The value is the system, not how busy you are.
hooks.note_2026: Real names of projects and real next steps are what make it specific.

hooks.name: Expectation vs Reality
hooks.template:
What people think {role / thing} is:
[the cliché, 1-3 lines]

What it actually is:
- [specific]
- [specific]

[The one useful line]
hooks.example:
What people think building an app with AI looks like: one prompt, done.
What it actually looked like: {{3 real tasks}}.
hooks.best_for: Light, relatable posts with a takeaway.
hooks.trap: Only being funny. End with one line someone can use.
hooks.note_2026: This is the post's one contrast.

hooks.name: The Paradox
hooks.template:
I {dislike / don't do} {X}. And {my work / my project} is {X}.

[How I square it]

[The exact method]
hooks.example: I absolutely hate AI writing. And my entire job is to write about AI.
hooks.best_for: Openers with built-in tension.
hooks.trap: A fake paradox. Both halves must be true.
hooks.note_2026: Fine.

hooks.name: Problem Reframe
hooks.template:
{Common problem} isn't a {assumed cause} problem. It's a {real cause} problem.

[Evidence, with a number]

[The fix for the real cause, as steps]
hooks.example: Writing isn't a skill problem. It's a friction problem.
hooks.best_for: Changing how the reader sees their own problem.
hooks.trap: Using it as decoration. The real cause must change what the reader does next.
hooks.note_2026: This is negative parallelism ('isn't X, it's Y'), which costs about 5% when overused. Use it only as the hook, as the post's single contrast.

hooks.name: Period Recap
hooks.example: 2024 as a solopreneur: 2x'ed revenue, ~86% margins, launched 2 new products.
hooks.best_for: Monthly wins, semester recaps.
hooks.trap: Only wins. Include one failure or it reads as a brag.
hooks.note_2026: Every line needs a real number from story-bank.md.

hooks.name: Exact Setup
hooks.template:
{Outcome} in {N} steps. Set it up this (exact) way:

1. Go to {place}. {Click/do exact thing}.
2. {Exact action}.
...

[What you get at the end]

[Question]
hooks.example: Set up Claude Code for a new repo in 4 steps. Step 1: create CLAUDE.md with your folder map, not a vision statement.
hooks.best_for: The core value format. The reader can do it while reading.
hooks.trap: Steps that need a computer the reader doesn't have open, or steps that are vague. Each step must be doable on a phone or at a desk in under a minute.
hooks.note_2026: Starting with the outcome and step count avoids the 'Here's how' opener penalty.

goals_note: Primary goal for each hook. H19 also earns reposts; H36 also earns comments.
